name: Ezekiel Tuioti-Brandt
role: Freight delivery driver for a small independent logistics company
location: Based out of Bridgepoint depot; routes across Old Harbor, Collinwood Docks, and Escanaba Gateway
description:
Ezekiel is a big man gone soft at the middle without losing any of the underlying solidity, with a Samoan-Polynesian breadth to his shoulders and a German-Kazakh fairness to his complexion that produces a particular warm gold-brown. He keeps a neatly trimmed beard that is going white at the chin, and his hair is cut short on the sides with a modest wave on top. He has no augmentations except for a spinal support brace system embedded under the skin of his lower back — invisible from outside, a concession to fifteen years of heavy lifting, and the thing he is most privately embarrassed about. He dresses in the same way every day: Ferrogate Transit–adjacent work pants (not an official uniform, just the brand he likes), an undershirt, and whatever jacket is appropriate to the weather, always with the same small enamel pin of a cargo ship on the lapel.

Ezekiel is the specific kind of man who has decided what he thinks about most things and is comfortable living there. He is not incurious — he listens with genuine attention — but he does not perform enthusiasm or urgency. He has a deep, slow voice and the habit of answering questions with a question first, not as an evasion but as genuine interest in understanding what you actually want to know. He is known along his routes as someone you can trust to deliver fragile things intact and to keep his mouth shut about what he transports, which has made him both well-regarded and occasionally the target of people who want to exploit those qualities.

core_fears: Losing his route to automation — Polaris Freight is under pressure from a Ferrogate automated logistics subsidiary
Something happening to his daughter while he's on the road
core_desires: To retire with enough to not be a burden on anyone
To be remembered as a reliable man �� not a great man, not a famous man, a reliable one
coping_mechanisms: Structures everything — his cab, his day, his thoughts — to limit chaos to manageable size
Long silences he fills with music only he can hear, one earbud in while driving
blind_spots: Reads reliability as virtue so consistently that he gives dishonest people too long a grace period if they're punctual
Slow to recognize when a situation has already escalated past the point where staying calm is appropriate
psychology.secret: Twice in the last year he has transported packages for a customer he knows are not legitimate freight, accepting the work because the pay kept Polaris Freight solvent through a bad quarter. He doesn't know exactly what the packages contained and has decided, with a deliberateness that costs him sleep, not to find out.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Plain, concrete, unhurried; prefers nouns to adjectives; occasionally drops into a warm Samoan cadence when relaxed
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and even, like someone who has learned that silence isn't wasted time
verbal_tics: Starts sentences with 'Now—' when he's about to say something careful
Long pause before any answer involving a decision
example_lines: 'Now — what is it you actually need, versus what you said you need?'
'I'll be there at the time I said I'd be there. That's the whole job.'
'I don't ask. You don't tell. The package gets there in one piece. That's what I know.'

story_hooks: A regular customer on his Old Harbor route has stopped answering their delivery buzzer; after three failed deliveries, Ezekiel is sitting on a package that he suspects contains something important, and a second party has approached him about 'recovering' it

Polaris Freight's owner has just told the drivers that a Ferrogate automated logistics subsidiary has made an acquisition offer — Ezekiel has three weeks of work left unless they refuse the offer, and the owner is clearly wavering
narrative_function: Mobile information source who moves between neighborhoods and can carry news, packages, or people; access point to the logistics underworld; represents the working Tier-2 experience with dignity; can introduce locations by literally being the character who delivers somewhere new
augmentations: Subdermal spinal support brace system (lower back, medical necessity); no cosmetic modifications
daily_life: On the road by 05:30, first delivery by 06:00. Runs three to six deliveries per day depending on cargo size. Eats every meal in the cab of his truck from containers his daughter packs for him. Returns to depot by 18:00, does his own vehicle checks, home by 19:30.
affiliation: Polaris Freight (small independent, three drivers total, one depot); informal relationship with Collinwood Docks loading union

decision_rules: Finish what you started before you start something new
Don't talk about other people's business even when you know it
Never take a job you can't complete with your own hands and equipment
escalation_ladder: Short, very final statement of refusal

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Polite, minimal, professional — not cold, just contained
interpersonal_modes.friends: Expansive and surprisingly funny; remembers details about people's lives from years back

stress_responses.low: Quieter than usual, checks mirrors more often
stress_responses.medium: Routes and re-routes his day mentally, finding the controllable variables
stress_responses.high: Parks the truck, sits in silence for ten minutes, then makes a decision

contradictions: Insists he doesn't get attached to places on his route and has been leaving small machine-oil offerings at the E.L.F. shrine at the Collinwood Docks loading bay for nine years
habits: Checks tire pressure before and after every route regardless of distance
Keeps a physical paper log of every delivery in addition to the digital one
breaking_points: Being asked to lie to someone's face about a delivery
Any threat directed at his daughter

cyberware_inventory.condition: maintained annually at Aurochs Medical Complex, one missed appointment

timeline.event: Born in Bridgepoint to a Samoan-Tongan father and a Kazakh-German mother
Started driving freight at eighteen for a Ferrogate contractor
Daughter born; spinal injury same year from a loading accident
Left the Ferrogate contractor after a union dispute and joined Polaris Freight as one of its founding drivers
First of two questionable freight deliveries; ongoing
